title: Alibi and Ledger
premise: Retired detective Freya Oyelaran has built a quiet life around a failing bookshop in the coastal town of Marrow Bay, solving only the deaths no one else would question—until twin letters arrive: one confessing to the drowning of her late husband's sister twelve years ago, the other promising that 'the ledger has more pages.' The confession is signed by the one person Freya once loved, forcing her to reopen the case everyone swore was closed while dodging a killer who knows her methods intimately. As the tide gives up what it took—a body, and with it proof of a second conspirator—Freya must choose between protecting the person she loved and the truth she owes the dead, ending with her exposing the real killer, closing the bookshop's ledger over the case for good, and finally letting herself be seen.
about_author: Theo Kavanagh is a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing coroner's records from England's drowned villages before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about people who thought they had escaped their pasts, and live within earshot of the sea they can't stop writing about.

chapters.title: Twin Letters
chapters.summary: POV: Freya. On a rain-slicked morning, Freya finds two letters in the bookshop post: one confessing to the drowning of Nell Oyelaran twelve years ago, signed by Daniel Ashworth—the man she loved before her marriage—and one unsigned, promising 'more pages to come.' The emotional beat is dread wrapped in longing; the past she buried has learned her address.

chapters.title: The Closed Book
chapters.summary: POV: Freya. She pulls her private file on Nell's death—ruled accidental, tide and drink—and rereads the inconsistencies she once chose to ignore because closure protected everyone, including herself. A visit from DS Imogen Pryce, who suspects Freya's anonymous casework, raises stakes. Emotional beat: guilt resurfacing like something washed ashore.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: POV: Freya, with an interlude from Daniel's letters. Walking the cove where Nell died, Freya notices erosion has exposed an old mooring ring—evidence someone anchored a boat there on a night Nell supposedly walked in alone. The second letter arrives, quoting her own unpublished notes verbatim. Beat: the hunter realizes she is also the hunted.

chapters.title: Ashworth
chapters.summary: POV: Freya. She tracks Daniel to a hospice two towns over, where he is dying and lucid enough to confirm he wrote the confession—but insists he didn't kill Nell; he covered for someone, and the second letter isn't his. He begs her not to dig. Beat: love against duty, sharpened by mortality; every answer costs her something.

chapters.title: Ledger Entries
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Freya and DS Pryce. Pryce confronts Freya with her anonymous case files, offering uneasy alliance instead of charges; together they trace the family money Nell was set to inherit, and find the estate ledger shows payments continuing after her death—to a name redacted. Beat: loyalty vs. truth begins splitting the town's old alliances.

chapters.title: The Bookshop Burns Slowly
chapters.summary: POV: Freya. An 'accidental' fire guts the back room where Freya kept her files; she saves the ledger page but loses Daniel's letters, and understands the arsonist wanted the confession destroyed, not her. A neighbor saw a figure wearing a coat like her late husband's. Beat: isolation deepening; grief weaponized against her.

chapters.title: Pages Missing
chapters.summary: POV: Freya. Following the redacted payments, Freya identifies the beneficiary: her brother-in-law Marcus Oyelaran, who inherited everything when Nell died and whose 'grief' funded the family home Freya still lives in. Confronted, Marcus produces an alibi—and Freya recognizes its phrasing as identical to Daniel's confession. Beat: the floor drops out; the alibi itself is the forgery.

chapters.title: Confession and Counterfeit
chapters.summary: POV: Freya and Daniel. Daniel admits Marcus dictated his confession years ago as insurance, to be sent if Marcus ever needed a scapegoat; the second letter came from Marcus, flushing out whether Daniel would stay silent. But Daniel reveals one thing Marcus doesn't know: Nell was alive when he left the cove. Beat: hope and horror entwined—the death may have been someone else entirely.

chapters.title: The Turning Tide
chapters.summary: POV: Freya. Storm surge exposes Nell's remains with a fractured wrist bone proving restraint, and fibers matching Marcus's old boat cover. Marcus, cornered at the cove where he finished what another began, tries to stage Freya's death as the fourth accident; Pryce, tipped by Freya's deliberate misdirection, takes him down as the tide turns. Beat: climax—truth overpowering loyalty, love forfeited to duty.

chapters.title: Closing the Ledger
chapters.summary: POV: Freya. In the aftermath, Freya testifies, visits Daniel in his final days without absolution but with honesty, and reopens the bookshop with a new shelf: cases the town got wrong. She signs her name to her casework for the first time. Beat: resolution—invisibility traded for integrity; the tide gives back, and so does she.
